headline: Large Energy User Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure for large energy users, such as data centers, away from residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocates, residential ratepayers, original bill sponsors.
opponents: Large energy users, data center industry, potentially Governor's office if amendments are seen as weakening the bill.
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics, including the bill's sponsor, expressed concern that the Governor's proposed amendments might weaken the bill's original intent to protect residential ratepayers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that data centers in Virginia report their water consumption to the state.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers.
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed Senate Bill 553, sponsored by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, to strengthen water-use reporting requirements for data centers. This legislation aims to provide better data on the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources, as data centers can use millions of gallons daily for cooling.

headline: Data Center Siting & Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes regulations for the geographical siting of data centers and imposes limits on their operational noise levels.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (due to increased regulatory burden).
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law: Siting and Noise Studies.
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of high energy use facilities, including data centers, to conduct site assessments examining their sound profile on nearby residential units and schools. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks, leaving some of those details to local discretion.
